title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: A classic Mediterranean salad made with ripe tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, red onion, Kalamata olives, and a slab of authentic Greek feta, finished with a traditional Greek vinaigrette.

ingredients.title: Fresh Vegetables
items: Ripe tomatoes – 3 medium (cut into irregular wedges, not cubes)
Cucumber – 1 medium (partially peeled, halved lengthwise, and sliced thick on a bias)
Red onion – ½ medium (thinly sliced into rings)
Green bell pepper – 1 small (thinly sliced into rings)
Capers – 1 tbsp (optional but adds authentic briny depth)

ingredients.title: Cheese
items: Greek feta cheese – 150 g (cut into a thick slab, not crumbled)

ingredients.title: For the Dressing (Classic Greek Vinaigrette)
items: Extra virgin olive oil – ¼ cup (high-quality, fruity)
Dried oregano – ½ tsp (plus extra for garnish)
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Vegetables
steps: Wash and pat dry all vegetables.
Slice as directed for visual variety—chunky, rustic cuts that retain texture.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Assemble the Salad
steps: In a large mixing bowl, combine tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, olives, and capers.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Dress the Vegetables
steps: In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
Pour over the vegetables and toss gently to coat evenly.
Allow it to marinate for 5–10 minutes for flavor absorption.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Plating (Restaurant Presentation)
steps: Place the tossed vegetables neatly in a chilled shallow bowl or on a flat plate.
Lay the slab of feta on top of the salad (not mixed in).
Sprinkle a little oregano and cracked black pepper on the feta.
Drizzle a touch of extra virgin olive oil over everything for shine.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Final Touch
steps: Garnish with a few fresh oregano leaves or microgreens for an elegant finish.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve chilled as a salad or appetizer.
Pairs well with grilled meats, seafood, or warm crusty bread.

chefTips: Always use ripe but firm tomatoes and cold, crisp cucumbers.
Never crumble the feta in an authentic Greek salad—serve it as a slab.
Chill the serving plate slightly before plating for a refined presentation.
For an elevated version, use PDO (Protected Designation of Origin) feta and single-estate olive oil.
